title: VACtívate: a proposal targeting conscious decision-making regarding vaccination in 20 cities in Colombia
Utility of ultrasound as a diagnostic tool for measuring knee cartilage thickness in patients with osteoarthritis: correlation with MRI
journal: Egyptian Journal of Radiology and Nuclear Medicine
abstract: Abstract Background Knee osteoarthritis (OA) requires precise cartilage evaluation for disease monitoring; however, MRI is constrained by cost and limited availability. Ultrasound (USG) offers a pragmatic, economical alternative. This study aimed to evaluate the correlation and agreement between USG and MRI in measuring medial femoral condyle cartilage thickness in patients with knee OA. Results MRI recorded greater mean medial femoral cartilage thickness (anterior: 1.35 mm, middle: 1.66 mm, posterior: 2.05 mm) than USG (anterior: 0.91 mm, middle: 0.97 mm, posterior: 0.99 mm). Strong positive correlations were observed between modalities across all regions ( r = 0.767–0.904, p < 0.001). Intraclass correlation coefficient (ICC) analysis demonstrated only moderate-to-poor absolute agreement (anterior ICC = 0.541, middle ICC = 0.416, posterior ICC = 0.264). Age was significantly associated with cartilage thinning; gender and BMI were not. Conclusions USG demonstrates strong correlation with MRI in measuring medial femoral cartilage thickness but consistently underestimates absolute values. It serves as a useful, accessible adjunct for cartilage assessment, particularly in resource-limited settings, while MRI remains the gold standard for precise morphological evaluation.

title: Towards atomic-level manufacturing: evolutions and perspectives
abstract: Abstract Atomic-level manufacturing (ALM) represents a critical evolution in manufacturing technology, extending the progression from macro- and meso-manufacturing to micro- and nano-manufacturing. As an advanced capability, it has the potential to transform materials science, serve as a foundational “root technology” for new industrialization, and is emerging as a key arena of global competition among manufacturing leaders. This review systematically explores the concept of ALM and its transformative impact on future industries. It first analyzes the essence and significance of ALM, emphasizing how precise and scalable control of atoms can revolutionize production by enabling atomic-precision manufacturing, atomic-scale structural fabrication, and ultimately the on-demand placement or creation of individual atoms. This review then discusses implementation effects and potential demand, highlighting broad application prospects in integrated circuits, quantum information, aerospace, and precision instrumentation. It also reviews technical systems and development status, focusing on the core elements that underpin ALM, including simulation and design software with supporting databases, atomic-level processing, atomic-level assembly, and atomic-level characterization, and summarizes representative domestic and international achievements and the major technical challenges across these areas. By examining contemporary products, the paper demonstrates practical ALM-enabled advances in fields such as novel materials and high-end sensors, illustrating its role in driving future industrial upgrading. In addition, it clarifies the distinctions and connections between ALM, integrated-circuit manufacturing, nano-manufacturing, and quantum technologies, thereby outlining ALM’s unique characteristics and development trajectory. Finally, the review traces the historical origins of ALM and assesses future breakthroughs, forecasting wide-ranging impacts on industry, the economy, and society.

title: The Multidimensional Impact of Chinese Population Mobility on Economic Development: Evolution And Contemporary Times
abstract: Since the founding of the People's Republic of China in 1949, large-scale and sustained internal population mobility has been a defining factor in the transformation of Chinese society. Through a multidimensional analysis and by identifying the historical stages of this mobility's development, this study systematizes the ways in which such movement has influenced China's economic development, social restructuring, and cultural integration, covering the entire chronological span from the planned economy era to the present day. The study aims to uncover the interrelationships between internal migration processes, economic modernization, and the evolution of China's cultural traditions. Central to the research is the hukou (household registration) system—the primary mechanism for regulating and constraining population mobility — and its gradual transformation. The study demonstrates how the evolution of internal mobility has laid the groundwork for key changes in China's economy and social development. Particular attention is paid to the changing nature of migration processes amidst the transition from a centralized planned economy to a market-oriented development model. The study examines the role of rural-to-urban migration in shaping the labor force, fostering industrial growth, and accelerating urbanization. It analyzes the impact of internal migration on the social structure, the widening of interregional disparities, the transformation of family dynamics, and the emergence of new patterns of social adaptation. Special emphasis is placed on the tensions arising from migrants' limited access to social services, education, and healthcare in host cities. Furthermore, the research explores the impact of migration on interregional cultural exchange, the spread of new values, and the interplay between traditional norms and modern social practices. On this basis, the study reveals the dual nature of internal mobility, which serves simultaneously as an engine of economic growth and a source of social tension. The results obtained provide a deeper understanding of the specific nature of the Chinese model of modernization and help determine the significance of migration processes for the country's future development.

“I Need Sleep Now”: A Qualitative Study of Sleep and Mothers of Autistic Individuals
abstract: ABSTRACT Objective This qualitative study examined the experiences of mothers of autistic individuals and how the autistic individual's sleep patterns influenced the mother's sleep and daily activities. Background Previous research has shown that sleep problems are common among the autistic population. When offspring have sleep issues, parental sleep is often interrupted, impacting multiple areas of functioning. Method We conducted a reflexive thematic analysis on interview data collected from 11 mothers of autistic individuals with sleep problems in the United States. Results Four themes were identified: it's never predictable, you're always on alert, I cannot sleep like this anymore, and sleep is the secret ingredient. These themes collectively show the interconnected nature between sleep disturbances experienced by autistic offspring and mother's sleep. Conclusion Guided by the family systems theory, sleep problems in autistic individuals affect the quantity, quality, and mental health of their mothers. The resulting chronic sleep deprivation causes difficulties engaging in everyday activities and social relationships. Implications Our findings reveal that when autistic offspring experience sleep problems, the family unit is affected. Service providers must be aware of the widespread effects sleep deprivation may have on family engagement and learning.
